title: Braised Red Cabbage
subtitle: Slow-cooked with apple, vinegar, and clove
excerpt: A British and northern European Christmas classic: red cabbage braised slowly with apple, brown sugar, cider vinegar, and warm spices until tender and deeply coloured. Makes ahead brilliantly and improves on standing.

recipe.sourceNotes: Braised red cabbage is a fixture of the British and northern European Christmas table, where it accompanies roast goose, duck, or pork. The sweet-sour combination of vinegar and sugar with warming spices reflects the Germanic influence on British festive cooking, particularly via the Victorian period when Prince Albert brought many German Christmas traditions to Britain. Red cabbage braised this way appears in the recipe collections of Elizabeth David, Jane Grigson, and Delia Smith as an indispensable make-ahead accompaniment. The dish benefits from being made a day or two ahead: the flavours deepen and mellow, and it reheats perfectly.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy-based saucepan or flameproof casserole with a tight-fitting lid.

content.text: Slice the cabbage finely: thick shreds take too long to soften and remain chewy. The acid from the vinegar and apple keeps the cabbage a vivid purple-red; without it the colour turns an unappetising blue. Cook with the lid on for the first hour, then remove it so any excess liquid reduces. Taste and adjust the balance of sweetness and acid at the end.

items.preparation: quartered, cored, and finely shredded (about 1 kg prepared weight)

content.text: Melt the butter in a large, heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the shredded cabbage and grated apple and stir to combine.

Add the sugar, cider vinegar, red wine vinegar, cloves, bay leaves, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Stir everything together and add 50 ml of water. Bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and cook over the lowest possible heat for 1 hour, stirring every 20 minutes.

Remove the lid and cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes until the cabbage is very tender and any liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze. Remove the cloves and bay leaves. Taste and adjust: add more sugar if too sharp, more vinegar if too sweet. Reheat gently before serving.
